label: D2: reached S2 while the agent is not committed to a2 (mainly a1 -> S2 rare)
explanation: Fires only at D2 and only when the state input is S2 (never on S1, D1 or GO). Within D2/S2 it fires when the agent is not strongly committed to a2: the model policy logit(a1)-logit(a2) at that step is > -1.5. Dev: P 0.89, R 1.00, F1 0.94. 86% of activation mass is the rare a1 -> S2 transition. The input-only predicate (phase == D2) & (in_state == 2) & (in_action == 1) gets dev P 0.94, R 0.77, F1 0.85. The rest is weak firing (about 0.2-0.4 of max) on common a2 -> S2 trials where the agent preference was near neutral. The logit is the agent own observed-time readout, not a future variable, but it is computed from the same hidden state, so it is partly circular. Magnitude on a1 -> S2 is largest (near max) when the previous trial was unrewarded (prev_reward 0) and lower (about 0.5-0.85) after a rewarded trial. It also tends to be larger on runs of a1 choices in S1-good blocks. It does not fire on S1 arrivals, a2 -> S1 rare trials, or any D1/GO step.

issues: The core claims hold on test. (phase==D2)&(in_state==2) has recall 0.99998 and mass recall 0.99999. Scored on their own, phase==GO, phase==D1 and D2&S1 each give recall 0.0, so the unit never fires outside D2/S2.

The original predicate reproduces on test: P 0.877, R 0.995, F1 0.932, mass recall 0.9996. The 275 test misses carry 0.0% of the activation mass (scattered weak firing on a1->S2 with a low logit). False positives are 8454 steps (about 12%), mostly common a2->S2 steps where choice is between -1.5 and -1.0 and the unit stays inactive, plus a few a1->S2 steps with no firing.

The -1.5 threshold is a bit loose. Moving it to choice > -1.0 gives test P 0.933, R 0.972, F1 0.952. A combined form, D2&S2&((in_action==1)|(choice>-1.0)), gets test F1 0.948 and mass recall 0.999. These are small refinements, not a different explanation.

'Mainly a1->S2 rare' holds by activation mass: 84% on test. By count of active steps it is weaker: a1->S2 makes up only 73% of active steps, so a2->S2 is about 27% of active steps (16% of mass). Within a2->S2 the firing is almost all after an unrewarded previous trial (recall 0.251 of the 0.270). But no observed-history predicate replaces the logit: the best tried, D2&S2&((in_action==1)|(prev_reward==0)), has test F1 0.71. So the logit term is needed, and it is partly circular, as the other agent said.

The magnitude claim that firing is stronger after an unrewarded previous trial is confirmed. On a1->S2, mass per step is about 2.3e-5 after an unrewarded trial vs 1.5e-5 after a rewarded one. The unscored claim that firing is larger on runs of a1 choices in S1-good blocks is NOT supported. good==1 and good==2 give about the same mass per step on a1->S2 (1.8e-5 vs 1.65e-5). After runs of rewarded a1, mass per step is lower (1.3e-5), and some test false positives are exactly that case: rare a1->S2 after 3 rewarded a1->S1 trials with near-zero activation. That remark should be dropped.
